Rashi on Pesachim 81a:11:1.hebrew: אין שוחטין וזורקין על טמא שרץ - ואשמעינן דטומא' התהום נמי דחיא ליה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:11:1.english: One may not slaughter and sprinkle for one impure from a creeping animal - And it teaches us that impurity of the deep also disqualifies him.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:12:1.hebrew: היכי משכחת לה - כיון דאית ליה מקצת היום עולה לה לספירתה, ומכאן ולהבא מטמאה, הו"ל כל יומא טומאה באנפי נפשה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:12:1.english: Under what circumstances is it found - Since he holds [that] part of the day counts toward her counting, and from then onward she renders [things] impure, each day is an impurity unto itself.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:13:1.hebrew: בשופעת - כל שלשה רצופין, דלא הוה לה מניינא כלל:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:13:1.english: In [a woman] who continuously flows - All three [days] consecutively, so that she had no counting [of clean days] at all.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:13:2.hebrew: אי נמי ברואה שני בה"ש - דכל תחלות הימים היו בטומאה, דאין כאן ספירה כלל, ובשני בין השמשות סגי, דאיכא טומאת ג' ימים רצופין. כגון בה"ש של ע"ש, יש כאן סוף ערב שבת ותחלת שבת, ובין השמשות של מחר, שהוא סוף השבת ותחלת א' בשבת — הרי ג' ימים רצופין, ואין כאן תחלת יום טהור שיעלה לספירה. ולפי הדברים, למ"ד מקצת היום ככולו, תחלת הלילה עולה לספירתה וא"צ עלות השחר, מדאיצטריך למנקט בין השמשות ולא נקט משכחת לה בשרואה בלילות:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:13:2.english: Or else, [the case is] where she sees [a discharge during] two twilights - For all the beginnings of the days were in [a state of] impurity, so that there is no counting [of clean days] here at all; and two twilights suffice, for there is impurity of three consecutive days. For example, [on] the twilight of Friday, there is here the end of Friday and the beginning of Shabbat; and [on] the twilight of the next day, which is the end of Shabbat and the beginning of Sunday — behold, [there are] three consecutive days, and there is no beginning of a clean day here that could count toward the counting. And according to [these] words, according to the one who says [that] part of the day is like the whole [day], the beginning of the night counts toward her counting and dawn is not needed, since [the Gemara] needed to state "twilight" and did not state, "you find it where she sees [a discharge] at night."

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:14:1.hebrew: בתמיד - כל השנה. ואליבא דמאן דאמר טומאה דחויה היא בציבור, קבעי רב יוסף הכי: אי איצטריך להדר אכהן טהור משום טומא' התהום, אי לא. ואליבא דמ"ד לקמן דטומאת התהום מרצי ציץ גבי נזיר ועושה פסח אפי' לכתחלה, כגון שנודע לו לפני זריקה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:14:1.english: With the daily offering - [of] the entire year. And according to the one who says [that] ritual impurity is [merely] overridden in [the case of] the community, Rav Yosef asks thus: whether it is necessary to seek out a ritually pure priest because of impurity of the deep, or not. And [this is] according to the one who says below that [with regard to] impurity of the deep, the frontplate effects acceptance for a nazirite and one who performs the Paschal offering even at the outset, such as where it became known to him before the sprinkling [of the blood].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:14:2.english: With their offerings - Of [the] nazirite and one who offers [the] Paschal lamb.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:15:1.hebrew: במקום שלא הותרה לו טומאה ידועה - כלל, כגון נזיר ועושה פסח, שהן קרבנות יחיד:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:15:1.english: In a place where known impurity is not permitted for him - [not permitted] at all, such as a nazirite or one offering the Paschal lamb, which are individual offerings.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:15:2.english: A place where known impurity is permitted for him - Where there are no ritually pure [people].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:1:1.hebrew: בשני שלה - עדיין ספק הוא, שמא תראה יום זה ויצטרף עם אתמול, ותראה גם מחר והוו להו שלשה, והויא לה זבה גמורה. ואם לא תראה, תטהר לערב:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:1:1.english: On her second [day] - It is still uncertain: perhaps she will see [blood] this day and it will combine with yesterday, and she will also see [blood] tomorrow, and there will be three [days] and she will become a full zavah. And if she does not see [blood], she will become pure in the evening.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:1:2.english: She may not eat - For tomorrow she still needs to be observing a [clean] day corresponding to a day [of discharge].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:1:3.hebrew: ופטורה מלעשות פסח שני - קס"ד, כיון דבשעת שחיטה וזריקה ספק הוי, מרצה ציץ מטומאת התהום דזיבה, ואע"ג דאיגלאי מילתא למפרע שנטמאה ודאי בטומאת התהום:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:1:3.english: And she is exempt from performing [the] second Pesach - [The Gemara] initially thought [that] since at the time of slaughter and sprinkling [of the blood] it was uncertain, the tzitz [High Priest's frontplate] effects acceptance for the impurity of the depths [unknown impurity] of zivah, even though the matter was revealed retroactively that she had definitely become impure with impurity of the depths.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:2:1.hebrew: מכאן ולהבא היא מטמא - שומרת יום כנגד יום שספרה קצת היום וטבלה, טהורה מטומאה של אתמול; וכי הדר חזיא בו ביום, מטמאה מכאן ולהבא, ותהיה מחר שומרת יום כנגד יום. הלכך, בזריקה ושחיטה טהורה מעלייתא הואי. ורבנן פליגי עליה, ואמרי דכי חזיא איגלאי מילתא למפרע דזיבה היא וחדא טומאה היא, ובשעת שחיטה ספק הואי, וחייבת בפסח שני. ולקמיה פריך: כיון דלר' יוסי כל חד וחד טומאה באנפי נפשיה הוא, היאך מצטרפים לזיבה לעשות זבה גדולה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:2:1.english: From now and onward she renders [objects] impure - A woman who watches a day for a day, who counted part of the day and immersed, is pure from yesterday's impurity; and when she sees [another discharge] again on that same day, she renders [objects] impure from now and onward, and tomorrow she will [again] be one who watches a day for a day. Therefore, at [the time of] the sprinkling [of the blood] and the slaughter [of the Paschal lamb], she was completely pure. But the Rabbis disagree with him, and say that when she sees [a discharge again], the matter is revealed retroactively that it is a zivah [discharge] and it is one [continuous] impurity, so at the time of slaughter she was in a state of doubt, and she is obligated in the second Pesach. And later [the Gemara] asks: Since according to Rabbi Yosei each and every [sighting] is an impurity unto itself, how do they combine for zivah to make [her] a major zavah?

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:3:1.hebrew: בעל שתי ראיות - דאילו בעל ג' ראיות לא חזי למיכל לאורתא עד שיביא קרבנותיו בח', ובשמיני נמי לא מצי למינקט ומיתני "ואח"כ ראה מטמא משכב ומושב למפרע", דכיון דיצא מזיבה ראשונה לשעה שהיא ראויה לקרבן, הויא לה הך זיבה אחריתי, ומושב ומשכב שמאתמול לאחר טבילה ועד הנה טהורה למפרע, אפילו טבלה בז' שחרית:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:3:1.english: Who has had two sightings - For whereas one who has had three sightings is not fit to eat [the Paschal lamb] in the evening until he brings his offerings on the eighth [day], and on the eighth [day] as well [the baraita] could not state and teach, "and subsequently he saw [a discharge], he renders objects for lying and sitting impure retroactively" — because since he already exited from the first zivah [period] to a time that is fit for an offering, this [new sighting] is [considered] a separate zivah, and any object for sitting and lying from yesterday after immersion until now is retroactively pure, even if she immersed on the seventh [day] in the morning.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:3:2.hebrew: משכבות ומושבות - שלאחר טבילתו טמאין, שהרי סתר מניינו והרי הוא כבתחלתו, דכתיב (ויקרא ט״ו:י״ג) וספר לו שבעת ימים — והרי אינן. ומדקתני נמי בשומרת יום למפרע, אלמא נמי למפרע מטמאה, ואפ"ה פטר לה מפסח שני, ש"מ טעמא משום דטומאת התהום הוי. ומשכבות ומושבות רבותא נקט להו, מפני שהן אב הטומאה לטמא אדם, ובדבר זה זב חלוק משאר טמאין:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:3:2.english: Objects for lying and sitting - [Those] after his immersion are impure, for he has invalidated his count [of clean days] and he is as [he was] at his beginning, as it is written (Leviticus 15:13): "And he shall count for himself seven days" — and behold, they are not [seven complete days]. And since [the baraita] also teaches regarding a woman who keeps a day [for a day] "retroactively" — thus [she] also renders [them] impure retroactively, and even so it exempts her from the Second Pesach — learn from this [that] the reason is because it is an impurity of the deep. And [the baraita] specifically mentioned objects for lying and sitting as a novel point, because they are a primary source of impurity to render a person impure, and in this respect a zav is distinct from other impure people.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:5:1.hebrew: מדרבנן - אבל מדאורייתא לא מטמאו אלא מכאן ולהבא, לא הזב בשביעי ולא שומרת יום בשני, דמקצת יום עולה להן לספירתן. הילכך, לגבי פסח טהורין מעליא הוו:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:5:1.english: By rabbinic [decree] - However, by Torah law, they do not become impure except from now and onward — neither the zav on [his] seventh [day] nor a woman observing a day [for a day] on [her] second [day] — for part of a day counts for them toward their counting. Therefore, regarding the Passover [offering], they are completely pure.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:6:1.english: But one who sees a zov discharge, etc. - We do not know to what [the word] "but" refers.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:6:2.hebrew: סותר את שלפניו - כל ספורין שספר, וצריך לספור ז' אחרים:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:6:2.english: It cancels that which preceded it - all the counted [days] that he counted, and he must count seven other [days].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:6:3.hebrew: וא"ל רבי יוחנן לא יסתור אלא יומו - ויחזור ויספור יום א'. והוינן אמילתיה דר' יוחנן: מה נפשך, אי למפרע מטמא, דאין מקצת היום עולה לו ולא נגמרה ספירתו:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:6:3.english: And Rabbi Yochanan said to him: It should cancel only its day - and he must go back and count one [more] day. And we [in the Gemara] ask on Rabbi Yochanan's statement: Whichever way you [look at it]: if [the zav] renders [objects] impure retroactively — because part of the day does not count for him and his counting was not completed — [it should cancel all of the days].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:1.hebrew: כולהו נמי נסתור - דכתיב: "וספר לו ז' ימים לטהרתו" — טהרה אחת לכולן, שלא תהיה טומאה מפסקת ביניהן, במס' נדה (דף לג:). ואם מנה לסירוגין כי הכא, שיסתור יומו וישלימנו למחר, נמצאת הפסקה ביניהם:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:1.english: It should also cancel all of them - For it is written: "And he shall count for himself seven days for his purification" — [meaning] one [continuous] purification for all of them, so that impurity should not interrupt between them, in Tractate Niddah (33b). And if he counted intermittently like here — that it would cancel its [own] day and he would complete it the next day — there would be an interruption between them.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:2.english: And if he renders [objects] impure from now and onward - For part of the day counted for him [as a full day], and his counted [days] were completed.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:3.hebrew: יומו נמי לא לסתור - אלא הרי הוא כראיה ראשונה של זיבה אחרת, ואין בה אלא טומאת ערב, ויטבול לערב ויטהר, דקי"ל ראיה ראשונה של זב קרי בעלמא הוא, במס' נדה (דף עב.):
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:3.english: It should not cancel even its own day - Rather, it is like a first sighting of another zivah, and it entails only impurity [until] evening, and he immerses toward evening and becomes pure, for we hold that the first sighting of a zav is merely [like] a seminal emission, in Tractate Niddah (72a).

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:4.hebrew: אלא - ה"ק ר' יוחנן: לא יסתור ולא יומו, כלומר אפילו יומו, לפי שכבר עלתה לו מקצת היום ככולו, ושלמו ספורין שלו, ויצא מכלל זיבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:7:4.english: Rather - This is what R. Yochanan is saying: "It shall not cancel, not even its own day" — that is to say, even its own day — because part of the day has already counted for him as the entire [day], and his counted [days] are complete, and he has left the category of zivah.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:1.hebrew: וא"ל - ר' אושעיא לרבי יוחנן:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:1.english: And he said to him - Rabbi Oshaya to Rabbi Yochanan.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:2.hebrew: ר' יוסי קאי כוותך - דס"ל נמי מכאן ולהבא הוא מטמא, מדפטר ליה לעיל מפסח שני. אלמא קסבר ר' אושעיא, למפרע דר' יוסי מדרבנן קאמר:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:2.english: Rabbi Yosei holds in accordance with your [opinion] - For he too holds [that] he renders [items] impure from now and onward, since he exempted him earlier from [bringing] the second Paschal offering. Thus, Rabbi Oshaya holds [that] Rabbi Yosei's [ruling of] "retroactively" was stated [as] a rabbinic [decree].

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:3.hebrew: והא ר' יוסי כו' - מסקנא דמילתיה הוא, ולא משום קשיא מייתי לה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:8:3.english: But [didn't] Rabbi Yosei, etc. - It is the conclusion of his statement, and he does not bring it as an objection.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:9:1.hebrew: השתא דאמר מכאן ולהבא מטמא - ולא משכחת טומא' התהום בזיבה:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:9:1.english: Now that he said [he] renders impure from now and onward - and [thus] you do not find impurity of the deep in [the case of] zivah.

Rashi on Pesachim 81a:9:2.hebrew: בלבד - דקתני לעיל, למעוטי מאי? ע"כ למעוטי שרץ תוקמא, ובכהן כדאמר לעיל, דאילו בבעלים לא מהני שרץ. וקאמר דבטומאת התהום דמת מיהא הותרה לו:
Rashi on Pesachim 81a:9:2.english: Alone - that was taught above: what [does it come] to exclude? Perforce, you must establish it [as coming] to exclude a creeping creature, and [speaking] of a kohen, as he said above — for regarding the owners, a creeping creature has no effect — and it says that in [a case of] impurity of the deep of a corpse, however, it is permitted to him.

Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:13:1.hebrew: אי נמי כגון ראתה שני ימים בין השמשות - מדלא משני ברואה בלילות, משמע דספירת לילה הויא ספירה, וכן פי' בקונטרס. וקשה לריב"א: דתנן פ' שני דמגילה (דף כ.): "וכן שומרת יום כנגד יום לא תטבול עד הנץ החמה", ומסיק בגמ': "קמ"ל כיון דבעי שימור, שימור ביממא הוא". וכן בשילהי נדה (דף עב.) אמר: "ושוין ברואה תוך י"א יום וטבלה לערב ושמשה, שמטמאים משכב ומושב וחייבין בקרבן", משמע אפילו לא ראתה אח"כ, ומשום דבלילה לא חשיב שימור! וי"ל דודאי ספירת לילה לא הויא ספירה, ומ"מ לא מצי לאוקמא ברואה בלילות, משום דכיון דסבר רבי יוסי מקצת היום שספרה בשביעי הוי ככולו, ה"ה אם פסקה בחצי היום שיעלה לה שימור סוף הנשאר; לכך מוקי בשופעת שלא היה סוף היום בטהרה, א"נ ברואה שני בין השמשות, וליכא למימר שיעלה לה אמצע היום שימור, דלא אמר מקצת היום ככולו אלא או תחלתו או סופו, אבל אמצע לא. וכן איתא בהדיא בנזיר בפ"ב (דף טו.) דקאמר: "ורבי יוסי זבה גמורה היכי משכחת לה? כיון דחזאי פלגא דיומא, אידך פלגא סליק לה שימור!" ומשני: "כגון דחזאי תלתא יומי סמוך לשקיעת החמה, דלא הוה שהות ביום דסליק לה ממנינא". ותלתא יומי לאו דווקא, דראיה שלישית לא חיישינן שתהא סמוך לשקיעת החמה, מאחר שכבר ראתה שני ימים סמוך לשקיעת החמה, ובשלישי תראה באיזו שעה שתהיה בלילה, ובלבד שתראה קודם היום, שלא יעלה לה שימור תחלת יום ג'. וא"ת: והא אמרינן בפרק בנות כותים (נדה דף לג.) דכותית יום שפוסקת סופרתו למנין שבעה, הא רבי יוסי נמי סבר הכא סוף היום ככולו! וי"ל דלא אמר סוף היום ככולו בתחלת חשבון אלא דוקא בסוף חשבון, כי הכא כגון זב בשביעי או שומרת יום כנגד יום, שאין לה למנות יותר; וסוף חשבון מסוף חשבון אית לן למילף, ולא מתחלת חשבון. ואשכחן חילוק בין תחלת חשבון לסוף חשבון בפ"ק דר"ה (דף י.): דנדה עולה לה סוף היום בתחלתה, ואין תחלת היום עולה לה בסופה, אע"ג דהתם הוי איפכא מסברתנו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:13:1.english: Or alternatively, [it is] a case where she saw [a discharge] during two twilights - From the fact that [the Gemara] does not answer [that it is a case] where she sees [discharges] at night, it is implied that counting [a clean] night is considered [valid] counting, and so Rashi explained. And this is difficult for the Riba: for we learned in the Mishnah in the second chapter of Megillah (20a): "And similarly, a woman who observes a day against a day may not immerse until sunrise," and [the Gemara] concludes in the Gemara: "[The Mishnah] teaches us that since she requires observation [of a clean day], observation is [valid only] during the daytime." And similarly, at the end of Niddah (72a), it says: "And they agree regarding one who sees [a discharge] within the eleven days [of zivah] and immersed in the evening and had marital relations, that they render a couch and a seat impure and are liable for a sin-offering" — which implies even if she did not see [a discharge] afterward, and because [observation] at night is not considered [valid] observation! And one can answer that certainly counting at night is not [valid] counting, and nevertheless [the Gemara] could not establish [the case] as one where she sees [discharges] at night, because since Rabbi Yosei holds that part of the day that [a zav] counted on the seventh [day] is considered like the whole [day], the same applies if she ceased [seeing blood] in the middle of the day — that the observation of the remaining end [of the day] would count for her. Therefore, [the Gemara] establishes [the case] as one who flows continuously, where the end of the day was not in purity; or alternatively, as one who sees [a discharge] during two twilights, and one cannot say that the middle of the day counts for her as observation, for [Rabbi Yosei] did not say that part of the day is like the whole [day] except [for] either its beginning or its end, but not the middle. And so it is stated explicitly in Nazir in the second chapter (15a), where [the Gemara] says: "And according to Rabbi Yosei, how can you find a full-fledged zavah? Since she saw [a discharge] for half the day, the other half counts for her as observation!" And [the Gemara] answers: "For example, where she saw [a discharge] for three days close to sunset, so that there was no time left in the day to count for her from the tally." And "three days" is not exact, for regarding the third sighting we are not concerned that it be close to sunset, since she already saw [a discharge] on two days close to sunset, and on the third [night] she may see [a discharge] at whatever hour it may be at night, provided that she sees before daytime, so that the beginning of the third day will not count for her as observation. And if you ask: Behold, we say in the chapter Benot Kutim (Niddah 33a) that a Cuthean woman counts the day on which she ceases [seeing blood] toward the tally of seven [days] — behold, Rabbi Yosei also holds here that the end of the day is like the whole [day]! And one can answer that [Rabbi Yosei] did not say that the end of the day is like the whole [day] at the beginning of a tally, but rather specifically at the end of a tally, such as here — for example, a zav on the seventh [day], or a woman observing a day against a day, who has no more [days] to count; and we should derive the end of a tally from the end of a tally, and not from the beginning of a tally. And we find a distinction between the beginning of a tally and the end of a tally in the first chapter of Rosh Hashanah (10a): that for a niddah, the end of the day counts for her at her beginning, and the beginning of the day does not count for her at her end, even though there it is the opposite of our reasoning:

Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:15:1.hebrew: אמר רבא ק"ו כו' מקום שהותרה לו טומאה ידועה אינו דין שהותרה לו טומאת התהום - וא"ת: ונימא דיו — מה טומאה ידועה לא הותרה אלא היכא דלא אפשר, ה"נ טומאת התהום? וי"ל: דעדיפא פריך, אפילו לר' טרפון דלית ליה דיו היכא דמיפרך ק"ו (בב"ק ד' כה.):
Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:15:1.english: "Rava said: [It is] an a fortiori inference, etc. ... in a place where known impurity is permitted for him, is it not right that impurity of the deep is permitted for him?" - And if you ask: Let us say dayo [it is sufficient for the derived law to be like the source]: just as known impurity was permitted only where it is impossible [to find a pure priest], so too impurity of the deep [should only be permitted where it is impossible]? One can answer: [The Gemara] asks a stronger [objection], [which holds] even according to Rabbi Tarfon, who does not hold of dayo where the a fortiori inference would be refuted (in Bava Kamma 25a).

Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:2:1.hebrew: לאו משום דסבר דציץ מרצה - תימה לרשב"א: מנ"ל? דילמא הא דפטורין היינו משום דסבר דנשים בשני רשות. ואור"י דבהדיא מוכח לקמן סוף פרק האשה (דף צא:) דרבי יוסי סבר נשים בשני חובה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:2:1.english: Is it not because he holds that the frontplate appeases - This is astonishing to the Rashba: how do we know [this]? Perhaps the reason they [women] are exempt is because he holds that [observing] the second [Pesaḥ] is optional for women. And R"I says that it is explicitly proven later at the end of the chapter [entitled] HaIshah (91b) that Rabbi Yosei holds [that] the second [Pesaḥ] is obligatory for women.

Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:2:2.hebrew: קסבר רבי יוסי מכאן ולהבא היא מטמאה - פי': ואנן סבירא לן כרבנן דלמפרע מטמאה. וא"ת: כי ס"ד נמי דטעמא דרבי יוסי משום דסבר ציץ מרצה, מאי פריך? לימא דס"ל כרבנן! וי"ל: שלא רצה לעשות מחלוקת חדשה, שלא מצינו תנאים חלוקים בכך; אבל בלמפרע הוא מטמא מצינו תנאים בשילהי נדה (דף עב.), אמתני' דטבלה יום שלאחריו ושימשה:
Tosafot on Pesachim 81a:2:2.english: Rabbi Yosei holds that she renders [objects] impure from now and onward - Explanation: And we hold like the Rabbis, that she renders [objects] impure retroactively. And if you will say: Even when it initially entered [our] mind that Rabbi Yosei's reason is because he holds that the frontplate appeases, what was [the Gemara] challenging? Let [him] say that he holds like the Rabbis! And one can answer that [the Gemara] did not want to create a new dispute, since we do not find Tannaim disagreeing about this; however, regarding [the issue of] rendering impure retroactively, we do find Tannaim [disagreeing] at the end of [tractate] Niddah (72a), on the Mishnah of "she immersed on the day after it and had marital relations."
